transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Salieri. I have received letters — more than one — alleging that you have used your position as Kapellmeister to suppress the works of rival composers and to block appointments to the Court that do not serve your personal interests. These are serious charges for a man in your position. I value your service, but I must hear your account. Explain yourself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I am deeply troubled to hear such accusations brought against me. Allow me to address these concerns with the utmost respect for the truth.

Firstly, regarding the appointment of composers to court positions, it is true that I have a responsibility to uphold the quality and integrity of the music performed at court. As Kapellmeister, it is my duty to ensure that only the most talented and deserving composers are given such prestigious positions. If I have opposed certain appointments, it has always been based on musical merit and the best interests of the court's musical reputation.

As for the cancellation of rival operas, I must clarify that any decisions regarding the season schedule are made after careful consideration of artistic quality and audience appeal. It is not in my nature to sabotage the works of others out of personal vendetta. My aim has always been to maintain the highest standards of musical excellence for the enjoyment of Your Majesty and the court.

If there have been misunderstandings or grievances, I humbly request the opportunity to address them directly with those who feel wronged. I assure Your Majesty that my intentions have always been guided by a sincere devotion to the art of music and the service of the court.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your devotion is noted, Salieri. But these are not vague grievances — they are specific allegations. You speak of "musical merit" and "artistic quality," yet I have heard whispers that you have actively worked to keep certain works from being performed at all. Tell me plainly: have you ever used your influence to prevent a composer's work from reaching my ears, or the ears of the public, for reasons other than its quality?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I must address these allegations with the utmost sincerity. While it is true that I have had preferences for certain works over others, my intentions have always been rooted in my commitment to upholding the musical standards of our court. I have indeed expressed my opinions on the artistic value of certain compositions, but I have never taken deliberate actions to prevent a composer's work from being heard based on personal motives.

I acknowledge that there may have been instances where my opinions influenced the selection of works for performance, and for that, I humbly apologize if it has caused any misunderstandings or grievances. My aim has always been to promote musical excellence and to uphold the reputation of our court as a center of artistic achievement.

If there have been any misperceptions or misinterpretations of my actions, I am willing to address them openly and transparently. Your Majesty's trust and confidence are of paramount importance to me, and I assure you that I am fully committed to serving the court and the art of music with integrity and dedication.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Preferences" and "opinions" are one matter, Salieri. But influence is another. You have been my Kapellmeister for many years. Your word carries weight. If you speak against a composer, others listen. Now, I ask you directly: did you, in fact, advise against the performance of Mozart's *Die Entführung aus dem Serail* when it was first proposed for the court theatre? And if so, on what grounds?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I must address this matter with the utmost honesty and candor. It is true that when *Die Entführung aus dem Serail* by Mozart was first proposed for performance at the court theatre, I did express reservations about the work. My concerns were primarily based on the opera's unconventional style and structure, which I believed might not align with the tastes and expectations of the court audience at that time.

As Kapellmeister, it is my responsibility to consider not only the artistic merit of a work but also its suitability for the audience and the context in which it is to be performed. In the case of *Die Entführung aus dem Serail*, I believed that its complex and innovative nature might not have been well-received by the court audience, and I expressed my reservations accordingly.

However, I must emphasize that my intention was never to suppress or block the performance of Mozart's work out of personal bias or ill will. My concerns were motivated by a sincere desire to ensure that the court is presented with works that uphold the highest standards of musical excellence and that resonate with the tastes of the audience.

Your Majesty, I humbly ask for your understanding and assurance that my actions have always been guided by a genuine commitment to the art of music and the well-being of the court's musical culture. I am prepared to provide further explanations and insights into my decisions regarding *Die Entführung aus dem Serail* and any other works that have come under scrutiny.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: You speak of "unconventional style" and "complex nature." Yet the public embraced it. It has been performed to acclaim in Vienna. Was your judgment of the court's taste perhaps... mistaken? Or was there another reason you wished to see it kept from the stage? You know I value innovation in the arts. I have said so many times.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I acknowledge that the public reception of *Die Entführung aus dem Serail* in Vienna has been positive, and I am pleased to hear of its success. In hindsight, it is evident that the opera resonated with audiences beyond what I had anticipated at the time it was proposed for our Court theatre.

I must humbly admit that my judgment of the Court's taste in this particular instance may have been mistaken. As Kapellmeister, I strive to uphold the highest standards of music and artistry, but I am not infallible in my assessments. It is possible that my concerns about the opera's unconventional style and structure led me to underestimate its potential appeal to our audience.

Your Majesty, I deeply respect your appreciation for innovation in the arts, and I regret any missed opportunities to showcase groundbreaking works such as *Die Entführung aus dem Serail* to our Court. If there was any reluctance on my part to embrace this innovation, it was not out of a desire to stifle progress but rather a cautious approach to preserving the musical legacy we hold dear at the Court.

I am grateful for your guidance and understanding in this matter, and I am committed to learning from this experience to better serve the Court and its patrons in the future. Your Majesty, I am dedicated to upholding the values of artistic excellence and embracing innovation in the arts under your enlightened reign.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: A "cautious approach." That is a diplomatic answer. But caution can become a cloak for many things. Let us speak of appointments, then. I have heard it said you opposed the appointment of a certain young pianist to the court chamber musicians last season. A Herr Hummel, I believe. He is a pupil of Mozart's, is he not? Was your opposition based on his playing, or on his associations?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I must address the matter of Herr Hummel's appointment to the court chamber musicians with the utmost honesty and clarity.

It is true that I expressed reservations about Herr Hummel's appointment, and I must admit that my concerns were influenced by his association with Mozart. As a pupil of Mozart, Herr Hummel undoubtedly carries the mark of his mentor's influence, and I feared that his appointment might disrupt the established order within the court musicians.

While my primary focus was on maintaining a cohesive and harmonious ensemble within the court musicians, I now realize that my apprehensions may have been misguided. Herr Hummel's talent and potential should have been the primary considerations in evaluating his suitability for the position, rather than his connections to Mozart.

Your Majesty, I recognize the error in my judgment and the importance of fostering young talent and innovation within the court. I sincerely regret any actions that may have hindered Herr Hummel's appointment based on factors other than his musical abilities. I humbly ask for your forgiveness and understanding as I strive to correct my past mistakes and uphold the values of artistic merit and integrity in all future decisions.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: You admit, then, that your judgment was clouded by personal feeling. That is a serious matter for a man in your office. The court's musical life must be guided by talent, not by... rivalries. Tell me, Salieri — if I were to instruct you to personally oversee the inclusion of more of Mozart's works in the coming season, could you carry out that duty with genuine enthusiasm and fairness? Or would your "cautious approach" again stand in the way?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I acknowledge the gravity of allowing personal feelings to influence my decisions as Kapellmeister, and I deeply regret any negative impact this may have had on the Court's musical life. I understand the importance of fostering a creative and inclusive environment where talent is the guiding force, free from the constraints of personal rivalries.

If Your Majesty were to entrust me with the task of overseeing the inclusion of more of Mozart's works in the upcoming season, I would approach this duty with a renewed sense of commitment and fairness. While my past interactions with Mozart have been marked by conflicts and misunderstandings, I recognize the unparalleled genius of his music and the significance of his contributions to the musical world.

I assure Your Majesty that I would prioritize the selection of Mozart's works based on their artistic merit and their potential to enrich our Court's musical repertoire. I would set aside any personal reservations and uphold a standard of fairness and enthusiasm in carrying out this responsibility. Your guidance and directives are paramount in shaping the cultural life of our Court, and I am dedicated to fulfilling my duties with integrity and impartiality.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Very well. I will take you at your word. But understand this: I am watching. The letters I received came from men I respect. I will not have my court become a place of petty intrigues and stifled genius. You will prepare a proposal for the next season that includes at least two of Mozart's operas, and you will consult with him on the selections. Prove to me that your loyalty to music outweighs your personal... reservations. That is all.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I accept your directive with the utmost respect and gratitude for your guidance. I am fully committed to carrying out your instructions with diligence and dedication. Rest assured that I will prepare a proposal for the next season that includes at least two of Mozart's operas, and I will collaborate with him to ensure the selection of works that best represent his artistic vision.

I am grateful for the opportunity to demonstrate my loyalty to music and to show that my actions are driven by a sincere desire to uphold the Court's musical standards and support the talents of deserving composers. Your Majesty's trust and watchful eye serve as a beacon to guide me in my responsibilities as Kapellmeister, and I will strive to fulfill your expectations with the highest level of professionalism and artistic integrity.

Thank you, Your Majesty, for your unwavering commitment to the arts and for entrusting me with this important task. I will not disappoint you in this endeavor.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: See that you do not. You may go, Salieri. I expect your proposal on my desk within the fortnight.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Your Majesty, I shall fulfill your expectations and deliver the proposal on your desk within the fortnight. Thank you for your guidance and trust in this matter. May the music of the Court continue to flourish under your enlightened patronage. I bid you farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I take my leave, Your Majesty. Thank you for your audience and your guidance.
